newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power rises on outage,firm gas prices.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power rises on outage,firm gas prices.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast continued to strengthen Tuesday amid an unexpected nuclear outage and higher natural gas prices, sources said.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to hover slightly above normal through Wednesday but then slip to below-normal levels as the weekend nears.

Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Wednesday moved into the $26.00-28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Monday's $20.50-22.00 trading range. Offers were heard as high as $30.00.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were steady to up slightly at $14.50-15.00 per MWh, market sources said.
Fueling the rise in prices was news that TVA's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power unit, in Spring City, Tenn., was shut again late Monday.
In its morning status report, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said the unit is expected to restart Thursday, but the company would not comment.

At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Wednesday delivery held mostly steady in the $22.50-23.50 per MWh range, as near-seasonable temperatures were expected to continue over the next few days.
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was still assessed at $14.00-14.50 per MWh.
In Florida, firm, peak prices on a 16-hour schedule were talked in the $21.00-22.00 range, but trading remained very light.
Separately, Virginia Power's 781 MW Surry 1 nuclear power unit, shut Friday due to a steam pipe leak, is still expected to return to the grid Wednesday morning.
Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, is now expected to resume power output mid-week.
Oconee units 1 and 3, shut since October and each generating 846 MW, are expected to restart in February.
All three units are in Seneca, S.C.
Adding to the market's strength were higher natural gas prices. Along the Gulf Coast pipes, prices rose by about five cents to the low-$3 per million British thermal units area.
